stages.title: MEANING AND CHRONOLOGY - NEOLITHIC, NEOLITHIC-CHALCOLITHIC AND CHALCOLITHIC — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: The safest chronology is regional and site-based rather than a subcontinent-wide start date.
stages.mechanism: Neolithic conventionally combines food production with ground, pecked and polished stone tools; many sites also show pottery and more sedentary settlement.
stages.consequence: Memory hook: NEO is not one date; CHALCO is not only copper; CULTURE is not ethnicity.
stages.trap: INFERENCE: Labels are useful for comparison but must be applied after examining local sequences.
stages.answer: Chalcolithic denotes the use of copper alongside stone, not an exclusive copper technology.

stages.title: TRANSITION FROM FORAGING TO FOOD PRODUCTION - MOSAIC, NOT LADDER
stages.terms: Transition is best understood as a changing portfolio of subsistence strategies.
stages.mechanism: Complex foraging and intensive use of wild plants could precede domestication.
stages.consequence: Mixed subsistence is normal, not transitional failure.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: transition is best understood as a changing portfolio of subsistence strategies.
stages.answer: Sedentism and food production are related but not identical.

stages.title: WHY DOMESTICATION? COMPETING EXPLANATIONS AND A MULTI-CAUSAL VERDICT
stages.terms: Environmental improvement can encourage domestication as much as crisis.
stages.mechanism: Environmental improvement can encourage domestication as much as crisis.
stages.consequence: Social motives such as feasting, exchange, inheritance and territorial claims may have mattered but are hard to recover.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: archaeologists have proposed environmental stress, nuclear-zone knowledge, demographic pressure, positive feedback from productive domesticates...
stages.answer: Upinder Singh treats the impulses behind domestication as regionally variable and difficult to isolate.

stages.title: DOMESTICATION OF PLANTS - DIRECT EVIDENCE, INDIRECT EVIDENCE AND RICE CAUTION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Cultivation is not identical to full domestication.
stages.mechanism: A crop package can combine local domestication, adoption and long-distance transfer.
stages.consequence: Cultivation is not identical to full domestication.
stages.trap: Domestication is not identical to economic dominance.
stages.answer: Plant presence is not identical to cultivation.

stages.title: DOMESTICATION OF ANIMALS - HERD STRUCTURE, MORPHOLOGY AND HUMAN CONTROL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: One small bone cannot establish domestication; assemblage pattern and secure identification are essential.
stages.mechanism: Mehrgarh shows declining wild gazelle and rising cattle, sheep and goat proportions through time.
stages.consequence: Burzahom retained hunting and fishing while also using domestic cattle, sheep, goat and dog.
stages.trap: One small bone cannot establish domestication; assemblage pattern and secure identification are essential.
stages.answer: Animal domestication is inferred from long-term morphological change, demographic profiles, geographic displacement, pathologies, residues and settlement context.

stages.title: POLISHED STONE, MICROLITHS, BONE TOOLS AND THE PERSISTENCE OF OLDER TECHNOLOGIES — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Polished Stone, Microliths, Bone Tools And The Persistence Of Older Technologies — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Polished Stone to Microliths, then testing the relationship through Bone Tools and The Persistence Of Older Technologies.
stages.mechanism: Tool choice depends on cost, repairability, raw materials and task suitability rather than a simple hierarchy of progress.
stages.consequence: Bone and antler industries were especially prominent at Burzahom and Chirand.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: use technological persistence to challenge stage-based determinism.
stages.answer: Technology layers overlap; polished stone does not erase microliths, and copper does not erase stone.

stages.title: POTTERY, COOKING, STORAGE AND CERAMIC CHRONOLOGY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Pottery supported cooking, serving and storage, but food production can precede pottery.
stages.mechanism: Ceramic seriation must be anchored by stratigraphy and absolute dates.
stages.consequence: Treat pottery as technology, chronology and social communication, while refusing to equate style with ethnicity.
stages.trap: Black-and-red ware is not one people or one date.
stages.answer: Pottery supported cooking, serving and storage, but food production can precede pottery.

stages.title: SETTLEMENT, HOUSES, STORAGE AND THE NEW TIME HORIZON
stages.terms: House size, internal divisions and settlement layout can suggest household differentiation.
stages.mechanism: House size, internal divisions and settlement layout can suggest household differentiation.
stages.consequence: Public works require coordination but do not by themselves prove a state.
stages.trap: Sedentism concentrates waste, pathogens and social tensions while also enabling craft and community institutions.
stages.answer: Explain settlement as a package of permanence, storage, property, public labour, health risk and social negotiation.

stages.title: SUBSISTENCE, LABOUR, HEALTH AND DEMOGRAPHIC CONSEQUENCES
stages.terms: Technically, Subsistence, Labour, Health And Demographic Consequences is analysed by relating Subsistence to Labour, then testing the relationship through Health and Demographic Consequences.
stages.mechanism: Food production increased carrying capacity but could distribute benefits unequally.
stages.consequence: More food does not guarantee better nutrition.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: population growth can be an outcome as well as a pressure.
stages.answer: Farming could raise aggregate food availability and support population growth, but early farmers often faced narrower diets, infectious disease, hard labour and vulnerability to drought, pests and storage loss.

stages.title: CRAFTS, SPECIALIZATION AND EXCHANGE NETWORKS
stages.terms: Technically, Crafts, Specialization And Exchange Networks is analysed by relating Crafts to Specialization, then testing the relationship through Exchange Networks and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: Use exchange to connect ecology with society: specialized zones traded complementary resources without necessarily forming one political system.
stages.consequence: Early villages were not isolated subsistence units.
stages.trap: Imported material does not prove political control.
stages.answer: Exchange can move raw materials, finished goods, people and ideas.

stages.title: SOCIAL DIFFERENTIATION, HOUSEHOLD ORGANIZATION AND SETTLEMENT HIERARCHY
stages.terms: Inamgaon has interpreted craft quarters, central elite structures and a settlement hierarchy.
stages.mechanism: Inamgaon has interpreted craft quarters, central elite structures and a settlement hierarchy.
stages.consequence: Differences in house size, settlement position, diet, burial treatment, stored wealth and craft location suggest emerging ranks at some sites, but inequality varied greatly and should not be read as a fully developed class state.
stages.trap: Use the phrase 'suggests ranked differentiation' rather than claiming kingship unless evidence is stronger.
stages.answer: Settlement hierarchy does not automatically equal state hierarchy.

stages.title: RITUAL, BURIALS, FIGURINES AND THE PROBLEM OF MEANING
stages.terms: Malwa and Jorwe contexts include fire installations, figurines and house-floor burials.
stages.mechanism: Malwa and Jorwe contexts include fire installations, figurines and house-floor burials.
stages.consequence: Inamgaon has unusual urn and symbolic burials as well as temporary clay figurines.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: burzahom has human and animal burials and a hunting engraving.
stages.answer: Ritual is inferred from patterned, non-utilitarian context.

stages.title: REGIONAL MAP IN TEXT - THE INDIAN NEOLITHIC MOSAIC — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Study link: Dedicated regional cases follow.
stages.mechanism: Similar tools may reflect convergent adaptation, interaction or shared learning; the mechanism must be tested.
stages.consequence: North-west is not the only early agricultural zone.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: study link: Dedicated regional cases follow.
stages.answer: South Indian ash mounds are not universal even within the south.

stages.title: NORTH-WEST NEOLITHIC - MEHRGARH AS A LONG SEQUENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Mehrgarh demonstrates that early village formation was already socially and economically complex.
stages.mechanism: Mehrgarh demonstrates that early village formation was already socially and economically complex.
stages.consequence: Mehrgarh was not a city in its earliest phases.
stages.trap: The 2025 radiocarbon revision must be presented alongside, not silently substituted for, older textbook chronology.
stages.answer: Use Mehrgarh as a sequence, not a label: subsistence, storage, craft, burial and exchange changed across periods.

stages.title: KASHMIR NEOLITHIC - BURZAHOM AND GUFKRAL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Burzahom is not famous for rock-cut shrines.
stages.mechanism: Burzahom Period I is known for round or oval pits, storage pits and ground-level hearths.
stages.consequence: Burzahom is not famous for rock-cut shrines.
stages.trap: DEBATE: Pits may have been dwellings, storage units or seasonally used structures; majority opinion is not proof.
stages.answer: Burzahom and Gufkral show pit structures, polished stone and bone tools, hunting and fishing, increasing cultivation and herding, distinctive burials and contacts beyond the valley.

stages.title: VINDHYAN FRINGES AND MIDDLE GANGA - KOLDIHWA, MAHAGARA AND LAHURADEWA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Lahuradewa later developed many earthen silos and wider crop-animal packages.
stages.mechanism: Lahuradewa later developed many earthen silos and wider crop-animal packages.
stages.consequence: These sites are central to debates on rice, cattle, continuity from the Mesolithic and the emergence of settled food-producing communities outside the north-west.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the regional Neolithic emerged from an established Mesolithic background and retained microliths.
stages.answer: Use the middle Ganga evidence to argue for regional experimentation while remaining cautious about claims of independent domestication.

stages.title: EASTERN INDIA - REPRESENTATIVE SEQUENCE
stages.terms: Other eastern sites show regional spread, but do not memorise an exhaustive inventory unless a specific option requires it.
stages.mechanism: Other eastern sites show regional spread, but do not memorise an exhaustive inventory unless a specific option requires it.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that other eastern sites show regional spread.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: other eastern sites show regional spread.
stages.answer: Chirand is the core exam anchor: a Bihar site with a long Neolithic-Chalcolithic sequence and bone-tool evidence.

stages.title: NORTH-EAST NEOLITHIC - REGIONAL CAUTION
stages.terms: Technically, North-East Neolithic - Regional Caution is analysed by relating North-east evidence to North-east, then testing the relationship through India and India.
stages.mechanism: Use it to reject an all-India sequence; do not turn corridor or extension hypotheses into settled site chronologies without a verified source.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that north-east evidence is regionally important but uneven.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: north-east evidence is regionally important but uneven.
stages.answer: North-east evidence is regionally important but uneven.

stages.title: SOUTH INDIAN NEOLITHIC - CHRONOLOGY, LANDSCAPE AND REGIONAL SEQUENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: South Indian Neolithic was not a copy of Mehrgarh.
stages.mechanism: The link between Mesolithic and Neolithic phases in the far south remains incompletely worked out.
stages.consequence: Ash mounds are regional, not universal.
stages.trap: Cattle were central, but recent botanical work demonstrates important millet and pulse cultivation.
stages.answer: South Indian Neolithic was not a copy of Mehrgarh.

stages.title: ASH MOUNDS - FORMATION, FUNCTION AND COMPETING INTERPRETATIONS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, Ash Mounds - Formation, Function And Competing Interpretations — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating Ash Mounds - Formation to Function, then testing the relationship through Competing Interpretations and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: Present the debate as a hierarchy of confidence: dung origin is strong; exact function and symbolism remain variable.
stages.consequence: Dung origin does not settle social meaning.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: utnur had pen enclosures and cattle hoof impressions.
stages.answer: Do not force one function on the entire class of sites.

stages.title: SOUTH INDIAN CASE RECALL
stages.terms: Retain one southern comparison: cattle-centred lifeways, polished axes and ash-mound traditions show a distinct regional trajectory.
stages.mechanism: Retain one southern comparison: cattle-centred lifeways, polished axes and ash-mound traditions show a distinct regional trajectory.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that extra site names are supporting detail, not a core inventory.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: extra site names are supporting detail, not a core inventory.
stages.answer: Extra site names are supporting detail, not a core inventory.

stages.title: REGIONAL NEOLITHIC COMPARISON - WHAT VARIED AND WHAT CONVERGED
stages.terms: Regional diversity persisted even as exchange networks widened.
stages.mechanism: Regional diversity persisted even as exchange networks widened.
stages.consequence: Shared outcomes do not require a single origin.
stages.trap: Ecology shapes but does not mechanically determine culture.
stages.answer: Conclude that the Indian Neolithic was a connected mosaic: multiple pathways, partial convergence and persistent regionality.

stages.title: CHALCOLITHIC INDIA - DEFINITION, GEOGRAPHY AND CULTURAL SEQUENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Major concentrations include Rajasthan, Malwa, Maharashtra, the Ganga plains and eastern India.
stages.mechanism: Major concentrations include Rajasthan, Malwa, Maharashtra, the Ganga plains and eastern India.
stages.consequence: Culture zones were networks of related material practice, not bounded political states.
stages.trap: Painted pottery is important but not exclusive.
stages.answer: Chalcolithic is not a uniform period.

stages.title: COPPER AND STONE TECHNOLOGY - ORE, SMELTING, ALLOYING AND SCARCITY
stages.terms: Inamgaon has evidence for copper extraction but copper remained scarce.
stages.mechanism: Control over ore and metal circulation could generate status without producing urban state power.
stages.consequence: Inamgaon has evidence for copper extraction but copper remained scarce.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: ahar has copper sheet and slag supporting local metallurgy.
stages.answer: Ganeshwar yielded over a thousand copper objects but published reports do not provide direct furnace evidence for the early phase.

stages.title: GANESHWAR-JODHPURA - COPPER ZONE, CRAFT CENTRE AND HARAPPAN CONTACT — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Ore-zone communities may have supplied both rural neighbours and urban Harappans.
stages.mechanism: A small site can be regionally important through specialization.
stages.consequence: Ore-zone communities may have supplied both rural neighbours and urban Harappans.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: the sequence shows movement from hunting with microliths toward extensive copper-working and wider interaction.
stages.answer: It is not a Harappan city.

stages.title: AHAR-BANAS CULTURE - RIVER VALLEYS, COPPER, FARMING AND SETTLEMENT DIVERSITY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Compare Ahar, Gilund, Balathal and Pachamta to show internal settlement hierarchy and changing organization.
stages.mechanism: Balathal fauna was dominated by domesticates, especially cattle, and crops were stored in bins.
stages.consequence: Compare Ahar, Gilund, Balathal and Pachamta to show internal settlement hierarchy and changing organization.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: shell and semi-precious materials indicate links to Gujarat and other zones.
stages.answer: White-painted black-and-red ware, copper use, mixed farming-herding and varied settlement sizes are major markers.

stages.title: KAYATHA CULTURE - EARLY MALWA SEQUENCE, WEALTH AND ABRUPT BREAK — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Kayatha is in the Malwa regional sequence.
stages.mechanism: The abrupt break could reflect conflict, ecological stress, mobility or other causes; evidence does not select one confidently.
stages.consequence: Use Kayatha to discuss wealth concentration, cultural contact and the difficulty of explaining archaeological breaks.
stages.trap: Absence of grain remains in excavation is not proof of no farming.
stages.answer: Kayatha culture in western Madhya Pradesh is an early Chalcolithic phase with fine wheel-made pottery, microliths, copper objects and concentrated bead wealth.

stages.title: MALWA CULTURE - NAVDATOLI, ERAN, NAGDA AND DECCAN SPREAD — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Malwa pottery is rich in form and motif.
stages.mechanism: Malwa culture followed Ahar in parts of central India and spread into the Deccan.
stages.consequence: Fire installations and decorated vessels have been interpreted ritually, but named-deity identifications are conjectural.
stages.trap: Malwa culture was a network spanning distinct local ecologies rather than a single homogeneous settlement system.
stages.answer: Navdatoli, Eran and Nagda are core Malwa sites.

stages.title: WESTERN DECCAN - SEQUENCE CAUTION
stages.terms: Technically, Western Deccan - Sequence Caution is analysed by relating Western Deccan to Deccan Sequence, then testing the relationship through Sequence Caution and Sequence Caution.
stages.mechanism: Use the region to explain non-linear change; do not memorise every ceramic phase for a general UPSC answer.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that western Deccan sequences show overlap and reorganisation across cultural labels.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: western Deccan sequences show overlap and reorganisation across cultural labels.
stages.answer: Western Deccan sequences show overlap and reorganisation across cultural labels.

stages.title: JORWE CULTURE - DISTRIBUTION, POTTERY AND SETTLEMENT HIERARCHY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Jorwe pottery has a red or bright-orange surface with black geometric painting.
stages.mechanism: Jorwe pottery has a red or bright-orange surface with black geometric painting.
stages.consequence: Large centres coordinated craft, exchange or storage, but regional political integration remains uncertain.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: use settlement hierarchy to discuss regional integration without overstating state formation.
stages.answer: Inamgaon is a key Jorwe site.

stages.title: INAMGAON - SELECTIVE CASE USE
stages.terms: In core answers, use it only to illustrate evidence-bound social differentiation.
stages.mechanism: In core answers, use it only to illustrate evidence-bound social differentiation.
stages.consequence: The resulting consequence is that inamgaon is a useful Deccan rural-lifeway case.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: inamgaon is a useful Deccan rural-lifeway case.
stages.answer: Inamgaon is a useful Deccan rural-lifeway case, but detailed household and rank reconstruction belongs to Optional Advanced depth.

stages.title: DECLINE AND TRANSFORMATION - LATE JORWE AND REGIONAL REORGANIZATION
stages.terms: Technically, Decline And Transformation - Late Jorwe And Regional Reorganization is analysed by relating Decline to Transformation - Late Jorwe, then testing the relationship through Regional Reorganization and Mains angle.
stages.mechanism: Use 'decline/transformation' rather than a single dramatic collapse unless evidence warrants it.
stages.consequence: Late levels show smaller huts, coarser pottery, reduced winter crops and greater reliance on hardy crops and wild resources.
stages.trap: Abandonment can mean mobility, reorganization or changed archaeological visibility rather than population disappearance.
stages.answer: Late Jorwe is not simply disappearance.

stages.title: OCP, COPPER HOARDS AND THE UPPER GANGA - ASSOCIATION WITHOUT ETHNIC LABELS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Hoards imply sophisticated metalworking but their users are difficult to identify.
stages.mechanism: Hoards imply sophisticated metalworking but their users are difficult to identify.
stages.consequence: Metal skill does not require nomadism or urbanism.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: use OCP to demonstrate the difference between an artefact horizon and a historically named...
stages.answer: OCP and copper hoards overlap but are not identical distributions.

stages.title: NEOLITHIC, CHALCOLITHIC AND HARAPPAN - RELATIONSHIP AND DISTINCTIONS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Daimabad includes a late Harappan phase within a longer Deccan sequence.
stages.mechanism: Daimabad includes a late Harappan phase within a longer Deccan sequence.
stages.consequence: Harappan demand may have stimulated rural resource specialization, but local agency remained important.
stages.trap: These formations overlap chronologically and interacted materially, but differ in scale, settlement hierarchy, craft organization, writing and urban institutions.
stages.answer: Chalcolithic communities were not failed Harappans.

stages.title: INTERPRETATIONS AND SOURCE LIMITATIONS - ARCHAEOLOGICAL CULTURE IS NOT A PEOPLE
stages.terms: New methods can change old interpretations.
stages.mechanism: New methods can change old interpretations.
stages.consequence: These are analytical constructs and cannot independently establish ethnicity, language, polity or migration.
stages.trap: Absence of evidence can reflect preservation or research history rather than ancient absence.
stages.answer: Culture names organize data; they do not speak for ancient identity.

stages.title: TRANSITION, NOT A SINGLE REVOLUTION
stages.terms: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.consequence: In a Mains answer, use "mosaic", "regional" and "overlap" to avoid replacing foragers with an instant farmer category.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: mehrgarh, Kashmir, the Ganga valley and south India are comparison points, not stages of...
stages.answer: Mehrgarh, Kashmir, the Ganga valley and south India are comparison points, not stages of one national ladder.

stages.title: WHAT COUNTS AS DOMESTICATION EVIDENCE? — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Technically, What Counts As Domestication Evidence? — [Core Prelims + Core Mains] is analysed by relating A seed, animal bone, tool or storage feature to It, then testing the relationship through Counts Domestication and Counts.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.consequence: It can support an inference about cultivation, herding or food processing; it does not automatically settle domestic status or economic dependence.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: it can support an inference about cultivation, herding or food processing.
stages.answer: A seed, animal bone, tool or storage feature is evidence only in context.

stages.title: REGION-SITE-MARKER TRIADS
stages.terms: Technically, Region-Site-Marker Triads is analysed by relating Mehrgarh--north-west--early to Burzahom--Kashmir--pit, then testing the relationship through Chirand--Bihar--long Neolithic-Chalcolithic and India--cattle.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.consequence: Do not add every excavated site unless it changes the option or argument.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: south India--cattle/polished axes/ash mounds.
stages.answer: Use compact triads: Mehrgarh--north-west--early farming; Burzahom--Kashmir--pit dwellings/bone tools; Chirand--Bihar--long Neolithic-Chalcolithic sequence; south India--cattle/polished axes/ash mounds; Ahar-Gilund--Banas valley--Chalcolithic; Malwa--Navdatoli/Eran/Nagda; Jorwe--Maharashtra.

stages.title: FROM PRODUCTION TO SOCIAL CONSEQUENCE
stages.terms: Technically, From Production To Social Consequence is analysed by relating A useful causal flow to From Production, then testing the relationship through Production Social and Production Social.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.consequence: The word "possible" matters: storage or a larger house can be a clue, not proof of a fixed hierarchy.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: storage or a larger house can be a clue, not proof of a fixed...
stages.answer: A useful causal flow is ecology/domesticates - cultivation or herding - storage and settlement routines - surplus/craft/exchange - possible differentiation.

stages.title: CHALCOLITHIC IS RURAL AND REGIONAL, NOT FAILED HARAPPA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.mechanism: A technological label names an archaeological pattern; it does not by itself name a people or a destiny.
stages.consequence: Compare them with Harappan urbanism only to explain differences in scale, settlement and material organisation; never use a culture label as an ethnic identity.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: it does not mean iron, automatic urbanism or a failed version of Harappa.
stages.answer: Chalcolithic means copper plus stone; it does not mean iron, automatic urbanism or a failed version of Harappa.
